title: Engineered 3D Silk-collagen-based Model of Polarized Neural Tissue
protocol: Cut each cocoon into 8 equal pieces using scissors.
Weigh 5 g of fragmented cocoons.
Prepare 2 L of 0.02 M Na2CO3 solution and bring it to boil.
Boil the fragmented cocoons in Na2CO3 solution for 30 min, stirring every couple of minutes with a spatula.
Wring the fibroin out by hand after boiling.
Rinse the fibroin in distilled water at least three times to wash out any remaining sericin and chemicals.
Place the wet fibroin on a petri dish.
Dry the fibroin extract in the flow hood overnight.
Weigh the dry fibroin mass the next day.
Calculate the volume of LiBr by multiplying the mass of dry fibroin by 4.
Pour LiBr solution over silk fibroin and immerse all fibers using spatula.
Cover the beaker and place it at 60 °C for 4 hr.
Collect fibroin solution from the beaker with a syringe and load into dialysis cassettes.
Perform dialysis against distilled water for 48 hr, changing water every couple of hours.
Collect fibroin solution from the cassettes using a syringe into conical tubes.
Centrifuge the collected solution twice at 9,000 rpm (~12,700 x g) at 4 °C for 20 min.
Pour supernatant into fresh tube after each centrifugation and discard pellet.
Measure concentration of fibroin by estimating dry weight.
Dry 1 ml of silk solution in an oven at 60 °C for 2 hr.
Weigh the dried silk fibroin and calculate its concentration by multiplying obtained weight by 100.
Adjust silk concentration to 6% (w/v) by diluting with distilled water if necessary.
Sieve granular NaCl to separate particles sized 500-600 µm.
Discard granules smaller than 500 µm and larger than 600 µm.
Pour 30 ml of 6% silk solution into a PTFE mold.
Gently scatter 60 g of sieved NaCl over the silk solution.
Tap the container to achieve an even layer of salt.
Incubate for 48 hours at room temperature to polymerize the silk.
Place the scaffold-containing PTFE mold in an oven at 60 °C for 1 hour.
Transfer the content of the PTFE mold into a beaker with 2 L of distilled water.
Change the water every 12 hours, up to 3 times daily for 48 hours.
Remove sponge scaffolds from the molds once all salt is leached out.
Store sponges immersed in water at 4 °C until further use.
Cut out scaffolds with a 5 mm diameter biopsy punch when ready.
Pre-cut scaffolds to reach approximately 2 mm in height.
Punch out the center of each scaffold using a 2 mm diameter biopsy punch.
Autoclave scaffolds immersed in water (wet cycle, 121 °C, 20 minutes) to sterilize them.
Immerse scaffolds in sterile 0.1 mg/ml poly-D-lysine solution before cell seeding.
Incubate the scaffolds for 1 hour at 37 °C.
Wash the scaffolds 3 times with phosphate buffered saline (PBS) to remove non-bound PDL.
Dissect cortices from embryonic day 18 (E18) Sprague-Dawley rats as previously described.
Incubate 10 cortices in 5 ml of 0.25% trypsin with 0.3% DNase I for 20 min at 37 °C.
Inactivate the trypsin by adding equal volume of 1 mg/ml soybean protein.
Triturate the cortices using a 10 ml Pasteur pipette by pipetting up and down 20 times until a single cell suspension is generated.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 127 x g for 5 min.
Re-suspend the cell pellet in 10 ml of culture medium (Neurobasal medium, 1x B27 supplement, 1x Glutamax, 1% penicillin/streptomycin).
Count the cells.
Move sterile scaffolds and all required utensils inside a cell culture hood.
Place the scaffolds in a 96-well cell culture plate with one scaffold per well using sterile forceps.
Immerse the scaffolds in cell culture medium to equilibrate them prior to cell seeding.
Incubate the scaffolds for 1 hr at 37 °C.
Aspirate excess medium from the scaffolds.
Apply 100 µl of cell suspension/scaffold.
Incubate cells at 37 °C overnight to allow cell attachment to the scaffold.
Aspirate the non-attached cells.
Apply 200 µl/well of fresh culture medium.
Place 10x PBS, water, 1 N NaOH and rat tail I collagen on ice.
Prepare a working solution of collagen as per manufacturer instructions.
Maintain the collagen solution on ice until cell-seeded constructs are ready (up to 1 hr).
Remove the cell-seeded silk constructs from the incubator.
Aspirate the excess medium from each construct.
Transfer scaffolds using sterile forceps to empty wells on the well plate.
Immerse each scaffold in 100 µl of 3 mg/ml collagen solution.
Place the tissue culture plate back in the incubator for 30 min to allow polymerization of collagen.
Apply 100 µl of pre-warmed cell culture medium/well.
Culture constructs for one week, changing the medium every day by replacing only half the volume of the medium.
Prepare stock solution of propidium iodide (PI) 1 mg/ml (1.5 mM) in distilled water.
Prepare stock solution of fluorescein diacetate (FDA) 2 mg/ml in acetone.
Dilute PI and FDA to prepare a working solution containing 10 µM PI and 0.15 µM FDA diluted in PBS.
Pre-warm the working solution to 37 °C in a water bath.
Wash cells with pre-warmed PBS to remove serum esterases.
Aspirate the PBS.
Apply the pre-warmed working solution on the cells for 2 min.
Wash cells with PBS.
Use epifluorescent microscope to image the cells (PI ex λ=490 nm, em λ=570 nm; FDA ex λ=490 nm, em λ=514 nm).
Fix the cells with 4% paraformaldehyde for 30 min at room temperature.
Wash scaffolds with PBS three times.
Incubate scaffolds in 0.2% Triton, 0.25% bovine serum albumin in PBS containing primary antibody overnight at 4 °C.
Discard the staining solution and wash scaffolds three times for 30 min each with PBS.
Incubate samples with secondary antibody diluted in 0.2% Triton, 0.25% BSA in PBS for 2 hours at room temperature.
Remove the staining solution and wash scaffolds three times for 30 min each with PBS.
Image scaffolds using a confocal microscope with a 20X objective by taking 100 µm z-sections of the sample with 1 µm step.
Using sterile forceps, transfer scaffolds out of culture plate into a 2 ml sterile tube.
Place one scaffold per tube.
Add 200 μl of RLT buffer to each tube.
Disrupt the construct by fragmenting it with sterile microscissors.
Transfer the content of the tube to the spin column for homogenization.
Spin for 2 min at full speed in a microcentrifuge.
Collect the flow through and use immediately to isolate RNA, DNA, and protein following manufacturer protocol.
Quantify nucleic acid yield using NanoDrop or another compatible method.
Quantify protein yield using BCA Protein Assay according to manufacturer instructions.
Measure assay outcome using microplate reader at wavelength 562 nm.
